promise: "We intend to designate this disaster as an 'Extremely Severe Disaster'" - all-out government support for Kumamoto earthquake recovery, including Cabinet reserve funds
description: On her first visit to quake-hit Kumamoto since the July 28 earthquake, Prime Minister Takaichi pledged all-out government support, said the government would designate the quake an 'extremely severe disaster' to raise state aid, and announced Cabinet approval of more than 20 billion yen in reserve funds on August 4. The Cabinet approved 24.2 billion yen in contingency spending on August 4, while the formal designation was still being prepared days later.
evidence: Cabinet approved 24.2bn yen in reserve-fund spending on Aug 4, 2026
Extremely severe disaster designation still being prepared as of Aug 5, 2026

promise: Present a national proposal to regulate cell phone and social media use in schools by the end of August 2026
description: The Sheinbaum government said it would define a national proposal by the end of August 2026 to regulate cell phone and social media use in schools, aimed at recovering attention, reading and learning in classrooms for the 2026-2027 school cycle.
evidence: Government timeline of 'end of August' set in early August 2026
Proposal tied to the 2026-2027 school cycle

role: Government of Hungary / EU Recovery and Resilience Facility
promise: Complete all milestones and targets required to unlock the full 10 billion euros in EU recovery funds by August 31, 2026
description: The Tisza government, elected in April 2026, is racing to document compliance with the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility milestones before the August 31, 2026 deadline to unlock about 10 billion euros in previously frozen funds (roughly 6.5 billion in grants and 3.5 billion in soft loans). Transport and Investment Minister David Vitezy said on August 15 the government was working to recover the full amount, including reapplying in Brussels after years of blocked funds under the previous government.
evidence: EU Council of Finance Ministers cleared the way on July 10, 2026; deadline for all milestones is August 31, 2026
Minister Vitezy confirmed the full 10 billion euro recovery target at the August 15 government briefing
